value.microspecies_note: The species that balances r_4273 as the GEM writes it is nitroethane (C2H5NO2, charge 0), NOT the ethylnitronate anion the GEM name claims. Verified with cobra check_mass_balance on yeast-GEM.xml: the reaction returns {} (balanced) with C2H5NO2 at charge 0. Hand check: LHS C19 H26 N5 O13 P1 charge -2; RHS C19 H26 N5 O13 P1 charge -2. Substituting the nitronate anion (C2H4NO2, charge -1) leaves the reaction short one hydrogen and one negative charge, and it re-balances only if the 2 H+ on the product side become 1 H+, which is exactly the form RHEA:28767 writes for EC 1.13.12.16. Nitroethane and its conjugate base are one compound in the eQuilibrator cache (compound id 1907), which carries both microspecies, charge 0 with 5 H and charge -1 with 4 H, separated by ddg_over_rt 20.838395091596116, i.e. a ChemAxon-predicted pKa of 9.05. The measured aqueous pKa is lower: 8.6 at 25 C (Wheland and Farr 1943), 8.46 at 25 C and 8.44 at 30 C (Turnbull and Maron 1943), all from the IUPAC compilation served by PubChem. Swapping the cache ladder for the measured pKa moves dfG'0 at pH 7.2 by 0.16 kJ/mol (181.71 to 181.55), which is far inside the group-contribution sigma of 3.97 kJ/mol, so the pKa is not what blocks this species.
value.representation_rule: Write an aliphatic or aromatic nitro group in the PENTAVALENT uncharged form N(=O)=O, never the charge-separated form [N+](=O)[O-], before handing a structure to the eQuilibrator group decomposer. The group definition -NO2 in group_definitions.csv has SMARTS [C,c,N,n]N(=O)=O and OpenBabel's matcher does not treat the two spellings as equivalent, so the charge-separated form leaves the nitrogen unassigned and the decomposition fails. Measured on this species: CCN(=O)=O decomposes with zero unassigned atoms into -NO2 + -C-[H2] + -C[H3] + Origin, while CC[N+](=O)[O-] (the SMILES ChEBI:16268 publishes) leaves atom 3 unassigned, and CC=N(O)=O (the SMILES the eQuilibrator cache stores for compound 1907) leaves atom 4 unassigned. Controls behave the same way: CN(=O)=O and c1ccccc1N(=O)=O decompose, C[N+](=O)[O-] and [O-][N+](=O)c1ccccc1 do not. The rule is reusable for every nitro species in the GEM, including s_3859 4-nitrophenyl phosphate and s_3860 4-nitrophenol. It fixes the DIAGNOSIS but buys no energy here, see notes.

notes:
WHICH SPECIES BALANCES r_4273. Nitroethane, C2H5NO2 at charge 0. cobra check_mass_balance on $DATA_ROOT/data/torchcell/yeast-GEM/yeast-GEM-9.0.2/model/yeast-GEM.xml returns {} for r_4273 exactly as the GEM writes it, with 2 H+ on the product side. The ethylnitronate anion (C2H4NO2, charge -1) does not balance that equation; it balances the variant with 1 H+, which is what RHEA:28767 writes for EC 1.13.12.16. So the GEM's formula and charge are self-consistent and only the NAME is wrong, and the GEM's two accessions disagree with each other: chebi=CHEBI:16268 is nitroethane while kegg.compound=C18091 is Ethylnitronate (C2H4NO2, ChEBI:55327). Biochemically the anion is the canonical substrate for EC 1.13.12.16, but the ExplorEnz comment records that the Neurospora crassa enzyme also turns over neutral nitroalkanes, so a yeast NMO homolog (YJR149W) acting on nitroethane is not absurd. Renaming s_3934 to nitroethane, or switching it to the anion and dropping one H+, is a GEM curation decision for a human, not something this record makes.

WHAT THE STRUCTURE FIX BUYS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It buys a correct diagnosis and nothing else. With CCN(=O)=O the decomposition succeeds and component contribution returns dfG0 = -31.17 kJ/mol, sigma_fin = 3.97 kJ/mol, and dfG'0 = 181.71 kJ/mol at pH 7.2, I = 0.25 M, T = 303.15 K, pMg 3.0; summing S^T dfG'0 over r_4273 with the proton at 0 gives -394.78 kJ/mol with sigma_fin 6.59 kJ/mol. That number MUST NOT be used. The -NO2 group is in the component-contribution null space: ||L_inf e_NO2|| = 1.0 and RMSE_inf = 100000 kJ/mol, verified two independent ways (the L_inf projection, and column 67 of train_G being used by 0 of the 631 training compounds). Both nitronate spellings are worse, since they route through [N]-O oxide groups that are also unconstrained. build_equilibrator_thermo.py already masks this correctly: its estimable flag is ||S^T sigma_inf|| < 1e-10, which is 1.0 here, so applying the structure fix would leave r_4273 with estimable = False. The integrating agent should therefore treat this record as a REPRESENTATION RULE plus a reclassification of the exclusion reason from group_decomposition_failed to unparameterized_group, not as a route to a price.

WHY THE CACHE FAILS AT ALL. eQuilibrator compound 1907 merges nitroethane, aci-nitroethane and ethylnitronate(1-) into one compound keyed on InChIKey MCSAJNNLRCFZED-UHFFFAOYSA-N and stores the aci spelling CC=N(O)=O. That spelling matches no group, so the cached group_vector is an empty list rather than None. That is a silent trap for any code that tests group_vector is not None as a proxy for decomposability, which thermo_structure_attempt.py does; an empty list passes that test and the failure then shows up one step later as a missing formation energy. Worth a one-line hardening there: test for a non-empty vector.

PKA. Not the blocker, but tabulated and measured, so recorded. The IUPAC compilation served by PubChem gives four aqueous values for the nitroethane / ethylnitronate couple: 8.6 at 25 C (Wheland and Farr, JACS 65, 1433, 1943), 8.49 at 18 C, 8.46 at 25 C and 8.44 at 30 C (Turnbull and Maron, JACS 65, 212, 1943), all by glass-electrode titration; the Turnbull and Maron entries are flagged as mixed constants at C = 0.003 to 0.007 M, and no ionic strength is stated. At the pipeline's 303.15 K the tabulated value is 8.44. The eQuilibrator cache carries a ChemAxon-predicted ladder of 9.05 (ddg_over_rt 20.838395091596116). Substituting the measured value changes dfG'0 by 0.16 kJ/mol at pH 7.2, so it would not be worth a separate pka_ladder record on its own for this species; it is recorded here so a later external-pKa pass can pick it up. If the integrator wants a standalone pka_ladder row: pkas [8.44], site assignment alpha C-H of the nitroalkane giving the C=N nitronate, T_K 303.15, ionic strength not stated.

DOCUMENTED NEGATIVES. No aqueous formation data. NIST Chemistry WebBook C79243 lists only liquid-phase dfH (-144.0 +/- 0.4, -143.6 +/- 1.1 and -140.1 +/- 1.3 kJ/mol) and combustion enthalpies, with no dfG, no aqueous phase, and an empty Henry's law table, so it cannot be turned into an aqueous Gibbs energy without a gas-phase entropy and a solvation model; that route would be computed, not measured, and was not taken. No TECRDB apparent equilibrium constant for a nitronate or nitroalkane reaction was found, and nitroethane is not among eQuilibrator's 631 reactant-contribution training compounds, which is the same statement from inside the tool. No entry surfaced in Alberty's tabulated reactant sets.

WHAT A HUMAN STILL NEEDS TO DO. Decide whether to rename s_3934 to nitroethane or re-specify it as the anion with 1 H+ in r_4273 (a GEM curation call). Decide whether r_4273 should simply stay unpriced, which is the honest outcome, or whether a nitro-group contribution should be fitted from an external source; the latter is a research task, since it requires aqueous data for at least one nitroalkane and none was found. Optionally harden the empty-group-vector test in thermo_structure_attempt.py, and apply the pentavalent-nitro representation rule to s_3859 and s_3860 as well, expecting the same unparameterized-group verdict.
